content:
For each odd integer \(m \le 2020\), consider the chain
\[
m,\;2m,\;4m,\;\dots \le 2020.
\]
Every number in \(\{1,\dots,2020\}\) belongs to exactly one such chain, determined by its odd part. Since any two numbers in the same chain divide each other, we can select at most one number from each chain.

The number of such chains equals the number of odd integers from \(1\) to \(2020\), which is
\[
\frac{2020}{2}=1010.
\]
So \(n\le 1010\).

This bound is attainable by choosing
\[
\{1011,1012,\dots,2020\}.
\]
No number in this set divides another, because twice any chosen number exceeds \(2020\).

\[
\boxed{1010}
\]
